note: Adapted from Sands' (1972) species-level description of Anenteotermes amachetus, originally in English; the species is soldierless, and the alate is based on a single queen whose colour was noted in the original as possibly faded; measurement-table headings, figure numbers, type locality and biological records are not translated, and numbers in the tables that are destroyed by OCR are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Among the alates, the species is one of three in which the posterior part of the head (behind the compound eyes) is not evenly rounded: A. cicur has shorter apical mandibular teeth, a less swollen postclypeus with the median suture and posterior margin very indistinct, and a markedly raised central spot; A. improcinctus has a broader constriction of the meso- and metathorax. In the worker the anterior tibia is hardly swollen and the third apical spur is reduced, which is diagnostic; the spines of the enteric valve appendages distinguish the species from A. cnaphorus, A. nanus and A. polyscolus, while the total absence of points on the scales distinguishes it from all the remaining species. The worker abdomen is of the dehiscent type.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule and pilosity yellow, setae sparse. Postclypeus moderately swollen, Pcl/W 0.29, Pcl/Ri 2.26. Apical teeth of the mandibles rather short, La/Li 0.70, Ra/Ri 0.84; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a distinct notch, composite ratio 18.10; first marginal tooth of the right mandible distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth shorter than that of the second, composite ratio 21.60. Anterior tibia hardly swollen, T1/Tw 5.00, the third apical spur reduced, less than one fifth the length of the other two spurs. Overlap of midgut and hindgut about three times the width of the midgut at the origin of the Malpighian tubules; enteric valve seat with two weakly developed opposing lobes and a smaller third endopad, connected by a distinct neck to the second paunch, dorsal in the unopened abdomen; endopads of the enteric valve all retracted, of roughly equal development, the surface scaly, the posterior margin of each scale with one or more minute points; membranous wall of the valve between and outside the pads with numerous minute spines arranged in curved rows.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule brown (from a queen, the colour possibly faded), darker above the ocelli; fontanelle small, less than half an ocellus, nearly flat, a faintly ridged oval, pale yellowish brown; central spot circular, smaller than the fontanelle, flat, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus yellowish brown, labrum yellow; frontal mark an indistinct flat yellowish brown crescent; antennae yellowish brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum yellowish brown, transverse sutures present; femora and tibiae pale yellowish brown, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites and dorsal spiracles yellowish brown, sternites and ventral spiracles pale yellowish brown, sternites paler medially, cerci yellow. Posterior margin of the head capsule faintly sinuate, not evenly rounded; ocelli medium-sized, the distance to the compound eye less than half their own minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately swollen, Pcl/W 0.28, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture present but weakly developed at both ends. Apical teeth of the mandibles short, La/Li 0.57, Ra/Ri 0.87; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible remote from the molar prominence in surface view, composite ratio 11.46; first marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margins of the marginal teeth about equal, composite ratio 21.30. Pilosity of the head capsule dense, slightly uneven, brown, almost a coarse felt, with projecting setae.
